excerpt: Hit by a big rig on US-17 / GA-25 through Broadfield in Glynn County? A Georgia truck accident lawyer's guide to deadlines, fault, and recovery.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a truck accident lawsuit after a US-17 crash in Glynn County?
faqs.answer: Under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33, you have 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal-injury lawsuit in Georgia. If a government vehicle was involved, ante-litem notice is required much sooner — 6 months for a city under O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5, 12 months for the state under O.C.G.A. § 50-21-26.

faqs.question: What if the trucking company says the crash was partly my fault?
faqs.answer: Georgia uses modified comparative negligence at O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, with a 50% bar. If you are found 49% at fault, you recover 51% of your damages. If you are 50% or more at fault, you recover nothing. Trucking insurers push this hard — reconstruction evidence and ECM data fight back.

faqs.question: Where will my Glynn County truck-accident lawsuit actually be filed?
faqs.answer: Most Glynn County personal-injury suits are filed in Glynn County State Court in Brunswick, part of the Brunswick Judicial Circuit. Larger or felony-adjacent cases go to Glynn County Superior Court. Federal cases with diversity jurisdiction file in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, Brunswick Division.

faqs.question: The truck driver had a Florida or out-of-state plate — does that change anything?
faqs.answer: Yes. Interstate trucking triggers the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (49 C.F.R.) on top of Georgia tort law, and the case may be removable to federal court. Out-of-state carriers also have to answer to USDOT compliance records, hours-of-service logs, and electronic ECM data that a Georgia attorney can subpoena early.

faqs.question: What if the truck driver who hit me was drunk?
faqs.answer: A DUI conviction under O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391 is persuasive evidence in your civil case and frequently supports a punitive-damages claim. If a Glynn County bar or restaurant over-served the driver before the crash, Georgia's dram-shop statute at O.C.G.A. § 51-1-40 may open a separate claim against the establishment.
